reply:
You don’t have to put it into words. If naming it would make it more real than it deserves, leave it unnamed.

What matters is that you already know it’s not true. The version she might drive home with is a guess she’d be making in the dark — not a verdict on you.

So maybe the move is small: give her one true sentence to hold instead of leaving her to invent one.

“Not avoiding the house — coffee near me just sounds easier this time. Want to?”

That doesn’t explain everything. It doesn’t have to. It just keeps the silence from doing all the talking.

What would make it easier to actually hit send?
